doc.title: DCA ATCT SOP
doc.summary: Standard operating procedures for Washington National (DCA) tower positions (CD, GC, LC, HC): runway configurations, clearances, altitude restrictions, departure gates and frequencies, departure headings, releases, missed approach and helicopter procedures.

items.title: Purpose, audience, cancellation and changes
items.text: Order vZDC-DCA-P-01D describes airspace, procedures and policy for all controllers working an operational DCA ATCT position on VATSIM; it applies to all vZDC controllers and visiting controllers training with vZDC. It is available at vzdc.org/publications/downloads and cancels vZDC DCA ATCT 7110.65C dated 1 July 2024. Changes are highlighted in grey; this version adds expanded Helicopter Local (HC) guidance, IDS departure release requests to TMU, and tower assumed radar identification procedures. Simulation use only.

items.title: Terms: arrivals, departures, delegated airspace
items.text: Arrivals and Departures refer specifically to aircraft on an IFR flight plan; VFR Arrival/VFR Departure refer to aircraft arriving/departing under VFR. Delegated Airspace is airspace assigned to a specific sector or position within a facility.

items.title: Abbreviations
items.text: ATAP Automated Terminal Proximity Alert; AOA at or above; AOB at or below; CHP Chesapeake Area of Potomac TRACON; CRC Consolidated Radar Client; FRZ Flight Restriction Zone; PCT Potomac TRACON; SFRA Special Flight Rules Area; STARS terminal radar software of vNAS/CRC; TDLS Tower Data-link System; vNAS Virtual National Airspace System; ZDC Washington ARTCC.

items.text: ATIS frequency 132.65.

items.text: CD combines to GC. GC combines to LC. HC combines to LC. The bold frequency (LC 119.1) is the primary frequency.

items.title: Non-standard runway configurations
items.text: Preferred configurations are North and South Operations. LC may use non-standard runway configurations as weather and traffic necessitate so long as it does not negatively affect traffic flow, is deemed necessary due to weather/traffic, and PCT is aware of the non-standard configuration.

items.title: North Ops: Rwy 1 primary; RJs on 4 and 33
items.text: Runway 1 is the primary arrival/departure runway. Regional jets or smaller may depart but not arrive runway 4. Regional jets or smaller may arrive or depart runway 33.
items.restr: Rwy 1 primary; Rwy 4 RJ-or-smaller dep only; Rwy 33 RJ-or-smaller

items.title: North Ops is the calm wind configuration
items.text: North Operation is the calm wind runway configuration. When the wind is less than 5 knots north operations should be used.

items.title: South Ops: Rwy 19 primary; RJs on 15; no RJ+ on 22
items.text: Runway 19 is the primary arrival/departure runway. Regional jets or smaller may arrive or depart runway 15. Regional jets or larger may not arrive or depart runway 22.
items.restr: Rwy 19 primary; Rwy 15 RJ-or-smaller; Rwy 22 no RJ or larger

items.title: Routine runway configuration change
items.text: The CIC determines the need for active runway changes; in a routine change departures may depart from the runway originally assigned. Provide PCT the last departure's identification, estimated time of departure and departure runway; after it departs, no aircraft departs DCA without a release from PCT. Ensure departures off the new runway have the appropriate SID and departure frequency; PCT informs the CIC when sector reconfiguration is complete; ensure the ATIS is updated.

items.title: Transponders with Mode C in movement areas
items.text: Ground Control and Local Control shall ensure all aircraft operating in a movement area have transponders on with Mode C.

items.title: ASDE-X configuration
items.text: Review FAAO 7110.65 Chapter 3, Section 6 (Airport Surface Detection Procedures). Configure the ASDE-X safety logic for either NORTH or SOUTH operations.

items.title: ASDE-X safety logic alerts
items.text: When an arrival (still airborne, prior to the landing threshold) activates a warning alert, issue go-around instructions. When two arrivals, or an arrival and a departure, activate an alert, issue go-around instructions or take appropriate action to maintain intersecting runway separation. For other alerts, use good judgment.

items.title: DC SFRA simulated procedures at DCA
items.text: DC SFRA procedures are simulated using a modified procedure. VFR departures are expected to file a DC SFRA flight plan. The FRZ does not impose higher requirements, so normal VFR operations including pattern work shall be allowed if workload permits. Ref: VATSIM DC SFRA Procedures and Pilot Guide; vZDC-PCT-P-01G Ch 2 Sec 8.
items.restr: VFR: file DC SFRA flight plan

items.title: Clearance Delivery responsibilities
items.text: CD formulates and issues IFR and VFR clearances to aircraft departing DCA, and reviews proposed flight plans for accuracy, amending routings and altitudes as necessary in accordance with appropriate LOAs.

items.title: Departures to constrained airports (EDCT/CFR)
items.text: For aircraft departing to a constrained airport (subject to a TMI such as EDCT or Call for Release), CD coordinates with the pilot for expected pushback/taxi time, submits a departure release request through IDS, advises the pilot of the anticipated wheels-up time, and ensures GC and LC are aware of it (considered coordinated when the correct release time shows in the IDS released aircraft list).

items.title: IFR departures: SID by direction, climb via
items.text: All IFR departures should be assigned a departure and transition consistent with their direction of flight. Climb via SID shall be used for all aircraft on a SID except the NATNL# departure.

items.title: NATIONAL SID (NATNL#): 5,000, filed alt 10 min
items.text: If an aircraft is unable to fly a SID, assign the NATIONAL-SID (NATNL#). Aircraft on the NATNL# departure are issued an initial altitude of 5,000 and to expect their filed cruise altitude ten minutes after departure (no climb via).
items.restr: Maintain 5,000; expect filed alt 10 min after dep

items.title: vTDLS pre-departure clearances
items.text: DCA is equipped with vTDLS to issue PDCs to IFR aircraft. TDLS shall be utilized for all eligible aircraft unless, in the controller's judgment, a voice clearance is more operationally advantageous. Ref: vZDC-A-01F para 4-1-4.

items.title: VFR flight following flight plan requirements
items.text: VFR aircraft requesting flight following shall have in their VFR flight plan prior to departure: destination airport, aircraft type, and requested VFR altitude.

items.title: VFR departures: Class B AOB 2,500 (fixed-wing)
items.text: All VFR departures shall receive a Class B clearance with a restriction to maintain VFR at or below 2,500 for fixed-wing aircraft. VFR aircraft remaining in the pattern are assigned a VFR code and do not require an altitude restriction.

items.title: VFR helicopter departures: Class B AOB 1,500
items.text: All VFR departures shall receive a Class B clearance with a restriction to maintain VFR at or below 1,500 for helicopters.

items.title: STARS VFR flight plan entry encouraged
items.text: Use of the STARS VFR flight plan entry function is encouraged.

items.title: North/East departures: KRANT 125.65
items.text: Assign departure frequency by SID, departure gate or direction of flight: North/East departures get KRANT (125.65). High altitude gates whose primary departure sector is KRANT (1K) per TBL 3-3-2: BUFFR, COLIN, JERES, PALEO, SWANN, WOOLY.

items.title: South/West departures: TYSON 118.95
items.text: Assign departure frequency by SID, departure gate or direction of flight: South/West departures get TYSON (118.95). High altitude gates whose primary departure sector is TYSON (1Y) per TBL 3-3-2: CLTCH, JDUBB, OTTTO, RAMAY, SCRAM.

items.title: IFR departure altitude restrictions (overview)
items.text: IFR aircraft destined to airports in TBL 3-2-1 are assigned an expected final cruise altitude per the table (by turbojet vs turboprop/propeller). Pilots may request higher with PCT or ZDC once airborne; it may be approved as an operational request.

items.title: DCA dep to BWI/IAD/HEF: 4,000 (all types)
items.text: Departures to BWI, IAD or HEF: turbojet 4,000; turboprop/propeller 4,000. Assigned as the expected final cruise altitude; pilot may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: DCA dep to EWR/TEB/LGA turbojets: FL210
items.text: Turbojet departures to EWR, TEB or LGA: FL210. Turboprop/propeller: N/A (no restriction listed). Assigned as the expected final cruise altitude; pilot may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: DCA dep to JFK turbojets: 17,000
items.text: Turbojet departures to JFK: 17,000. Turboprop/propeller: N/A (no restriction listed). Assigned as the expected final cruise altitude; pilot may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: Departure gates required for IFR departures
items.text: PCT uses departure exit gates for IFR departures to destinations outside PCT airspace. Every IFR aircraft leaving DCA must leave PCT airspace bound for one of these gates unless coordinated otherwise.

items.title: High altitude gates for aircraft filed above 10,000
items.text: High altitude departure gates should be used for aircraft filed above 10,000 feet. Prop and turboprop aircraft may be routed via a low altitude gate regardless of altitude. Ref: vZDC-PCT-P-01G para 6-4-11.

items.title: Low altitude gates for aircraft AOB 10,000
items.text: Low altitude departure gates should be used for aircraft filed at or below 10,000 feet. Low altitude aircraft may receive vectors to join any low altitude airway.

items.title: Low gate CSN: W/SW
items.text: DCA low altitude departure gate CSN, routing/direction W/SW. For aircraft filed at or below 10,000 feet (props/turboprops may use a low gate regardless of altitude).

items.title: Ground Control responsibilities
items.text: GC sequences departures to meet release restrictions and balance departure fixes, keeps runway exits clear for landing aircraft (coordinating with LC to have arrivals avoid exiting at unavoidably congested taxiways), and ensures transponders are on during all ground operations.

items.title: Multiple runway crossings authorized locations
items.text: Multiple runway crossings are authorized at: RWY 4/22 and RWY 1/19 at TWY Hotel; RWY 4/22 and RWY 1/19 at TWY Foxtrot; RWY 15/33 and RWY 1/19 at TWY Mike. Blanket crossings are not allowed.

items.title: Runway crossing coordination with LC
items.text: GC scans the TDW, final approach course and runways before requesting or issuing crossings. Coordinate by stating the runway and intersection (or "Westside"), number of crossings and traffic if applicable; GC advises LC when complete by stating clear of the runway crossed. Phraseology: CROSS RUNWAY (number), AT (intersection), (number of times), (traffic if necessary); e.g. "Cross RWY 4 at Juliet, three times" ... "Clear of RWY 4."

items.title: Runway 4/22 and 15/33 release to Ground
items.text: LC may release Runway 4/22 and/or Runway 15/33 to GC; LC must then ensure aircraft landing Runway 01/33 (as printed) do not exit onto the released runway. GC may only use a released runway to cross aircraft; GC coordinates with LC before holding an aircraft on it. LC may recall the runway at any time.

items.title: Runway assignment; non-standard needs LC coord
items.text: Assign runways based on traffic flow that ensures operational efficiency. Assigning a non-standard runway requires coordination with Local Control via verbal or nonverbal methods.

items.title: Pushback procedures
items.text: Movement areas: approve pushbacks onto taxiways and specify tail direction. Non-movement areas: provide pushback advisories into alleys, assign spots as needed (Appendix C), and provide traffic advisories into or out of non-movement areas; this is advisory only and does not imply control responsibility.

items.title: GC area: movement areas west of all runways
items.text: Ground Control is responsible for movement areas west of all runways as depicted in Appendix A.

items.title: GC hold bays: Rwy 15 and Rwy 4
items.text: Ground Control may use the runway 15 and runway 4 hold bays as necessary to comply with TMI requirements or at the request of Local Control.

items.title: B757 taxiway limitations
items.text: B757 type aircraft are not authorized to taxi on TWY November between TWY Kilo and the RWY 15 Hold Bay, or on TWY Whiskey (printed "TWR Whiskey"); aircraft may access the Hold Bay from TWY B.
items.restr: B757: no TWY N (K to RWY 15 hold bay), no TWY W

items.title: Local Control airspace (Appendix B)
items.text: Local Control is responsible for the airspace depicted in Appendix B (LC AOB 1500). When Helicopter Control is not online, Local Control assumes Helicopter Control airspace.

items.title: LC area: movement areas east of active runways
items.text: Local Control is responsible for movement areas east of all active runways as depicted in Appendix A.

items.title: LC hold bays: Rwy 19, 1, 33, 22
items.text: Local Control may use the runway 19, runway 1, runway 33 and runway 22 hold bays as necessary to comply with TMI requirements.

items.title: Certified tower radar display, quick looks
items.text: Data transfer between the tower and PCT is permitted using prescribed entries in this SOP or the PCT SOP. LC and HC must quick look DCAFR (1V), TYSON (1Y) and KRANT (1K), or the sector those are combined to, at all times. Automated pointouts between PCT and DCA ATCT are permitted when the datablock accurately reflects what the aircraft is doing; coordinate verbally if there is potential confusion.

items.title: Non-SID IFR heading North Ops: turbojets 320
items.text: For DCA departures not cleared via a SID, North Operation: turbojets fly heading 320 (both TYSON and KRANT departure sectors).

items.title: Non-SID IFR heading North Ops: props 280/090
items.text: For DCA departures not cleared via a SID, North Operation: props fly heading 280 to TYSON or heading 090 to KRANT.

items.title: Non-SID IFR heading South Ops: turbojets 190
items.text: For DCA departures not cleared via a SID, South Operation: turbojets fly heading 190 (both TYSON and KRANT departure sectors).

items.title: Non-SID IFR heading South Ops: props 230/150
items.text: For DCA departures not cleared via a SID, South Operation: props fly heading 230 to TYSON (and shall be instructed to maintain 3000) or heading 150 to KRANT.

items.title: VFR departure North Ops, North/East: heading 090
items.text: VFR departures in North Operations with a north/east direction of flight are issued heading 090.

items.title: VFR departure North Ops, South/West: NW over river
items.text: VFR departures in North Operations with a south/west direction of flight are instructed northwest over the river.

items.title: VFR departure South Ops: south over the river
items.text: All VFR departures in South Operations are instructed south over the river.

items.title: Line up and wait (LUAW)
items.text: Landing clearances need not be withheld for traffic holding in position. LUAW must not be used unless the aircraft will depart in three (3) minutes; LC may use LUAW when the aircraft is expected to depart after conflicting traffic clears the runway/intersection, using memory aids as needed. ASDE-X and all safety logic systems must be operational and used by LC.

items.title: No LUAW on Runway 22
items.text: LUAW procedures are not authorized on Runway 22.

items.title: Automatic departure releases and suspension
items.text: Automatic departures are authorized; aircraft subject to a TMI (EDCT or call for release) must depart within their release validity period. Automatic departures are suspended until PCT restores them when: there was a previous missed approach/go around and PCT has not given automatic releases back; PCT cancels automatic releases; or an aircraft is departing a non-standard (non-ATIS advertised) runway.

items.title: Calling PCT for release: required info
items.text: When any suspension condition applies, Local Control must call PCT for release stating: ACID; runway and departure heading; SID and transition or initial fix.

items.title: Tower assumed radar ID before switching to departure
items.text: Before switching a departure to PCT, the DCA local controller must observe the aircraft acquire on the STARS TDW within one mile of the departure end of the runway. If acquisition does not occur, notify the PCT departure controller before the frequency change, giving callsign and SID or assigned heading.
items.restr: Track acquired within 1 mi of DER

items.title: Autotrack by primary departure sector
items.text: The primary sector providing departure service uses autotrack for all DCA departures. If KRANT (1K) and TYSON (1Y) are decombined, the sector expected to service the majority of departures (e.g. event traffic) uses autotrack.

items.title: Reduced separation 2.5 NM - Runway 01 arrivals
items.text: Separation of IFR arrivals may be reduced to 2.5 NM within 10 NM of the runway on the final approach course, for Runway 01 arrivals only, assuming increased separation requirements (e.g. wake turbulence) do not exist.

items.title: Missed approach/go around coordination
items.text: LC shall immediately coordinate with PCT when a missed approach/go around occurs and, unless otherwise coordinated, issue instructions per TBL 5-3-2. Automatic releases are suspended until released by PCT. Tower may re-sequence props if it ensures separation from the go around and other pertinent traffic and does not affect PCT's IFR arrival sequence.

items.title: Go around North Ops: 3000, heading 320
items.text: Missed approach/go around in North Operation: altitude 3000, heading 320. Aircraft south of the DCA VOR/DME shall maintain 2,000 until over the airport to avoid ADW departures.
items.restr: 3000, hdg 320 (S of DCA VOR: 2,000 until over airport)

items.title: Go around South Ops: 3000, heading 185 or RH
items.text: Missed approach/go around in South Operation: altitude 3000, heading 185 or runway heading (RH).

items.title: Taxi arrivals across all runways before GC
items.text: Once aircraft are clear of the runway, they shall be taxied across all other runways prior to handing off to Ground Control.

items.title: Rwy 19 arrivals: exit Rwy 22, right on Juliet
items.text: Local Control may use runway 22 as a high-speed exit for aircraft arriving Runway 19. Aircraft should be instructed to turn right on taxiway Juliet before handing off to Ground Control.
items.restr: Exit via Rwy 22, right on J

items.title: Rwy 1 arrivals: exit Rwy 33, left on Sierra/November
items.text: Local Control may use runway 33 as a high-speed exit for aircraft arriving Runway 1. Aircraft should be instructed to turn left on taxiway Sierra or November before handing off to Ground Control.
items.restr: Exit via Rwy 33, left on S or N

items.title: Helicopter Control area of jurisdiction
items.text: HC operates within LC-designated airspace under prearranged coordination and is responsible for the airspace in Appendix B (HC AOB 1499). Helicopter operations are authorized on all movement areas; helicopters arriving/departing an area on the airport must be coordinated with GC and LC as appropriate before authorizing the operation.

items.title: HC duties: separation, helicopter routes, P-56
items.text: HC separates VFR traffic from DCA arrivals and departures, issues safety alerts and traffic advisories, clears VFR aircraft on routes or into zones per the Baltimore-Washington Helicopter Route Chart, and issues instructions to keep unauthorized aircraft clear of P-56.
items.restr: Keep unauthorized aircraft clear of P-56

items.title: HC frequency changes, codes and datablocks
items.text: Authorize a frequency change when the aircraft approaches the outer limits of DCA airspace. Ensure aircraft squawk assigned codes and validate Mode C within the DCA Class B. In DCA ATCT delegated airspace, helicopter datablocks must be taken to the appropriate tower position on initial contact (CRC uses the automated handoff function; no override modify), and track control/communications transferred when exiting DCA ATCT airspace.

items.title: HC required coordination; handoffs to IAD ATCT
items.text: HC coordinates with GC and LC as necessary for departures or arrivals within a movement or non-movement area; arriving helicopters may need to be handed to LC for landing clearance. HC airspace borders IAD ATCT airspace, and HC shall initiate radar handoffs to IAD ATCT as needed.

items.title: HC prearranged coordination in LC airspace
items.text: Prearranged coordination may be applied by HC in LC airspace and is considered accomplished when: both LC and HC use the TDW (STARS) display; HC ensures separation from all tracked or non-tracked targets in LC airspace except as authorized by LC; and operations follow the BWI/DCA Helicopter Route Chart (Appendix D). Route scratchpads (primary "Y" scratchpad, TBL 6-2-3) may be used at LC/HC discretion.
